traits.flowering_months.note: Kearney and Peebles, Flowering Plants and Ferns of Arizona (1942) p. 949, Zinnia pumila: dry mesas and slopes, commonly in caliche soil, April to October; FNA: flowering spring-fall.

traits.fruiting_months.note: A model estimate (confidence medium), as no source read gives it: cypselae ripe May to November, a month behind the flowers.

appearance.note: By eye, from the photos the traits cite: a low, rounded cushion of stiff, much-branched grey-green stems and needle-like leaves, dotted with small white-rayed heads with yellow centres. Colours set by eye were written as screen (sRGB) shades; they are read as the linear light a colour field holds, and bark and foliage follow the stated colour traits by rule (2026-10-19).

generator.params.note: Set by hand for desert zinnia from its sources and the photos the traits cite; the rest of its growth comes from the library's rules for the form. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: 0.12 m tall at 5 years in the open, within its sources' range, as grown. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.
